Allenyl Sulfones Mediated by Ion Pair Organocatalysis
Léo Birbaum, Moussa Ndiaye, Mahmoud Hachem, Stéphane Perrio, Michael De Paolis,*
and Isabelle Chataigner*

ABSTRACT: We report the first example of dearomative (3 + 2)
cycloadditions of 3-nitro(aza)-indole, -benzofuran, and -benzothio-
phene derivatives in the presence of allenyl sulfones, using sulfinate
ammonium ion pairs as organocatalytic promoters. The method-
ology provides a new, facile, and eficient protocol for the synthesis
of functionalized 2,3-fused cyclopentannulated indolines and
dihydrobenzofurans.

synthesis, generating three-dimensional (3D) molecules
from easily accessible raw substrates.<sup>1</sup> However, the disruption
of the stable aromatic π system makes their development
challenging from both kinetic and thermodynamic viewpoints.
In this context, electron-rich indoles have been used in many
alkaloid syntheses, taking advantage of their C3 nucleophil-
icity.<sup>2</sup> In a complementary way, N-protected 3-nitroindoles
have recently become privileged scafolds, with their C2�C3
double bond displaying an electrophilic behavior akin to
nitrostyrenes.<sup>3</sup> In the presence of electron-rich 1,3-dipoles,
several dearomatizing (3 + 2) cycloadditions have been
reported with 3-nitroindoles, allowing elegant generation of
tricyclic indolines.
The addition of catalytic phosphines to allenoates generates
1,3-dipoles, which can react with Michael acceptors to form α-
and/or γ-regioisomeric cyclopentenes (Scheme 1A, top).<sup>5</sup>
Recently, it has been shown that nitroheteroaromatics also
react with these dipoles to generate cyclopentaindolines, with
an exclusive α-regioselectivity (Scheme 1A, bottom).<sup>6</sup>

exhibit distinct reactivity in (3 + 2) annulations in the presence
of a sulfinate promoter (Scheme 1B).<sup>7,8</sup> This sulfinate is
incorporated into the cycloadduct, while a sulfinate anion
derived from the starting allenyl sulfone is released. As a result,
sulfinate can be used in catalytic amounts if it is similar to the
sulfonyl group on allene. These (3 + 2) annulations have been
extended to a few classical (hetero)dipolarophiles, including
acrylonitrile, methyl ketones, cyclic carbonyl compounds, or
imines.<sup>9</sup> Noteworthy, employing a sulfinate−ammonium

beneficial, expanding the scope of this chemistry to a broader
range of substrates.<sup>9e−h</sup>

In conclusion, we have developed the first dearomatization
of 3-nitroheteroarenes with allenyl sulfones to generate
fused cyclopentannulated heterocycles bearing a versatile
vinylsulfone motif. The process is catalyzed by sulfinate
anions, whether added or in situ generated, associated with a
quaternary ammonium salt. Unsubstituted or α-methyl allenyl
sulfones led to the exclusive or favored formation of the α-
regioisomeric cycloadducts, while the less reactive more
hindered α-ethyl allenyl sulfone furnished exclusively the γ-
regioisomer in reaction with 7-aza-3-nitroindole. The mecha-
nism, supported by a DFT study, suggests a highly energetic
sulfonyl anion formation, followed by a two-step cycloaddition
and a barrierless sulfinate release. The reactivity of
azanitroindoles is especially interesting to exploit, revealing
3D molecules that are pharmaceutically relevant. The diferent
derivatizations conducted further demonstrate the versatility of
these cycloadducts. We are currently looking to extend the
methodology to enantioselective processes through use of
chiral ammonium salts.
